body: Forward test of the flags-judgment context method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.22 (naive base rate 0.30) that: Payoneer's FY2026 10-K concludes internal control over financial reporting is effective (the Q3-2026 material weakness is remediated). Evidence: Q3 2026 10-Q: after the Q2 10-Q, management 'identified an error in Financial income (expense), net', corrected out-of-period (not restated); identified a material weakness in operating effectiveness of related controls; disclosure controls 'not effective' at 30-Sep-2026; remediation 'will require validation and testing of the operating effectiveness of internal controls over a sustained period of financial reporting cycles… timing… is uncertain'. Q3 2026 release (5-Nov-2026): revenue $276.9m (+2%), revenue ex-interest +5%, volume +13%, B2B volume +59%; pending merger with Nuvei (stockholders approved 14-Sep-2026; targeted mid-2027 close) and recent executive-management changes. Reasoning: The flag itself is low-teeth for the business (an out-of-period financial-income error), but the question is timing: only one quarter of testing is available before year-end, management's own language warns of 'sustained period' testing, and attention is on the Nuvei merger and leadership changes. We go below the base. Resolution: YES if Payoneer's 10-K for fiscal year ended 31-Dec-2026 states ICFR was effective as of 31-Dec-2026 and the material weakness disclosed in the Q3 2026 10-Q is remediated, with no new material weakness. NO otherwise, including if no 10-K is filed by 31-Mar-2027. Source: SEC EDGAR — Payoneer Global FY2026 Form 10-K, Item 9A. Resolve by 2027-03-31; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: Reference class (unverified): material weaknesses first disclosed in a Q3 10-Q are reported remediated by that fiscal year's 10-K only about a third of the time or less.

title: Paper call: Payoneer's FY2026 10-K concludes internal control over financial reporting is effective (the Q3-2026 material weakness is remediated)
